purpose: Third surface-authorship sensitivity pilot: keep the matched Dharma Connection leave-one-source-group-out design from PR #67 while equalizing every train and held-out document to one deterministic 50-word window, so each author contributes exactly 300 training words per fold.

fold_training.joel_rule: two non-heldout Joel-only Dharma supplement documents plus all Joel matched-queue documents except the current held-out source group
fold_training.control_rule: the same six largest explicit-speaker non-overlap Dharma profile documents per control selected before normalization, preserving the PR #67 document-selection rule

length_normalization.reason: PR #67 balanced six documents per author but Joel supplied only about 776-1276 training words per fold versus 9525 for David Vardy and 12119 for Stian Gudmundsen Høiland. This test removes that text-mass asymmetry without changing source groups or candidate authors.

interpretation.comparison_target: Compare directly with the matched-platform whole-document result in state/IDIOLECT-SURFACE-SVM-MATCHED-PLATFORM-CV-RESULT-2026-08-18.json. If character-based Joel attribution remains poor after exact text-budget equalization, document-length/profile-mass imbalance is not sufficient to explain the weak surface signal and surface SVM should be deprioritized as the operational calibration target. If it improves materially, expand the length-normalized evaluation before drawing any idiolect conclusion.
interpretation.stop_rule: Do not repeatedly tune window size/position against these same ten held-out documents. This 50-word centered window is a precommitted sensitivity test, not a hyperparameter search.
